He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. Washington was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. ==High school career== Washington played basketball for [[Cesar Chavez High School (Phoenix, Arizona)|Cesar Chavez High School]] in [[Phoenix, Arizona]]. As a sophomore, he averaged 23.2 points, 4.1 assists, 4.4 rebounds, and 3.3 steals per game.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=TyTy Washington ready to make hoops history at Cesar Chavez |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/11/14/tyty-washington-ready-make-hoops-history-cesar-chavez/4195597002/ |website=[[The Arizona Republic]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=November 14, 2019}} Washington transferred to AZ Compass Prep School in [[Chandler, Arizona]] during his junior season.{{cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |date=December 26, 2019 |title=Cesar Chavez hoops moves on without star TyTy Washington, routs Tempe |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2019/12/26/chavez-moves-without-star-washington-rout-tempe/2752449001/ |access-date=June 28, 2021 |website=The Arizona Republic}} As a senior, he averaged 24 points, seven assists, and six rebounds per game, leading his team to a 30–2 record.{{cite web |last=Tucker |first=Kyle |title=After his decommitment from Creighton, TyTy Washington is blowing up — and could head to Kentucky |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2520093/2021/04/14/after-his-decommitment-from-creighton-tyty-washington-is-blowing-up-and-could-head-to-kentucky/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=April 14, 2021}} He was named to the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] roster.{{cite web |last=Lindsey |first=Eric |title=Three UK MBB Signees Selected to Jordan Brand Classic Roster |url=https://ukathletics.com/news/2021/5/23/mens-basketball-three-uk-mbb-signees-selected-to-jordan-brand-classic-roster |website=University of Kentucky Athletics |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=May 23, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Washington was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top [[point guard]]s in the 2021 class. On November 15, 2020, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]].{{cite web |last=Nyatawa |first=Jon |title=Four-star guard TyTy Washington commits to Creighton |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/creighton/four-star-guard-tyty-washington-commits-to-creighton/article_e7272b4b-e4ea-510f-882d-7348e2b66a68.html |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]] |access-date=June 28, 2021 |date=November 15, 2020}} He decommitted on March 11, 2021. On May 12, 2021, Washington committed to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] over offers from [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] and [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364853 |access-date=January 10, 2022}} On January 15, Washington scored a career-high 28 points in a 107–79 win against [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]].{{cite news |title=Washington helps No. 18 Kentucky rout No. 22 Tennessee |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401364871 |access-date=January 16, 2022 |work=ESPN |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 15, 2022}} As a freshman, Washington averaged 12.5 points, 3.9 assists, and 3.5 rebounds per game. He was named to the Second Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] as well as the All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/33453309/men-basketball-all-sec-teams-awards-announced|title=Men's Basketball All-SEC Teams & Awards Announced |publisher=[[Southeastern Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} On April 6, Washington declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web|title=Kentucky freshman guard TyTy Washington Jr. entering NBA draft, plans to hire agent|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33683968|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|authorlink=Adrian Wojnarowski|work=ESPN|date=April 6, 2022|accessdate=April 6, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Houston Rockets (2022–2023)=== Washington was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 29th overall pick in the [[2022 NBA draft]]. The Grizzlies traded Washington and [[Walker Kessler]] to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] on draft night for [[Jake LaRavia]]. The Timberwolves subsequently traded Washington to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Wendell Moore Jr.|Wendell Moore]]. On October 2, 2022, Washington made his preseason debut, registering eight points along with three rebounds and one assist in a 134–96 win against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=San Antonio Spurs vs. Houston Rockets - NBA Box Score - October 2, 2022|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401474847|website=ESPN.com|access-date=October 4, 2022}} On July 8, 2023, Washington was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in a five-team trade.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Usman Garuba, Tyty Washington Jr., Future Draft Picks and Cash Considerations|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-usman-garuba-tyty-washington-jr-future-draft-picks-and-cash-considerations|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} On July 12, he was traded again, this time to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], along with [[Usman Garuba]], [[Rudy Gay]] and a 2026 second-round pick, in exchange for [[Patty Mills]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Usman Garuba, Rudy Gay, Tyty Washington Jr. and 2026 Second-Round Draft Pick|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-trade-230712|website=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2023|access-date=July 13, 2023}} On August 18, he was waived by the Thunder.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Thunder Waive TyTy Washington Jr.|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/08/thunder-waive-tyty-washington-jr.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=August 18, 2023|access-date=August 19, 2023}} ===Milwaukee Bucks (2023–2024)=== On August 29, 2023, Washington signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks sign TyTy Washington Jr. to a two-way contract|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-tyty-washington-jr-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 29, 2023|access-date=August 30, 2023}} ===Phoenix Suns (2024–2025)=== On August 2, 2024, Washington signed a two-way contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=SUNS SIGN TYTY WASHINGTON JR. TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-sign-tyty-washington-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 2, 2024|access-date=August 2, 2024}} He made 16 appearances for Phoenix during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 2.2 points, 0.8 rebounds, and 1.0 assists. On October 14, 2025, Washington signed a training camp contract with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He was waived prior to the start of the regular season on October 18.{{cite web | last=Simon | first=Dean | title=Clippers officially waive 6-foot-9 ex-Warriors forward, G-League superstar guard | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-10-19 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/clippers-officially-waive-6-foot-143002955.html | access-date=2025-12-06}} === Los Angeles Clippers (2025–2026) === On December 27, 2025, Washington signed a two-way contract with the Los Angeles Clippers{{Cite web |title=Clippers' TyTy Washington: Receives two-way deal |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/clippers-tyty-washington-signs-two-way-deal-with-clips/}} following a great season with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]].{{Cite web |title=Stats |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/1631102/}} ===ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne (2026–present)=== On August 24, 2026, Washington signed with [[ASVEL Basket|ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne]] of the French [[LNB Élite]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |title=Tyty Washington rejoint LDLC ASVEL |url=https://ldlcasvel.com/tyty-washington-rejoint-ldlc-asvel/|website=ldlcasvel.com|access-date=24 August 2026|date=24 August 2026|language=fr}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2022}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2022–23 Houston Rockets season|Houston]] | '''31''' || '''2''' || '''14.0''' || .363 || .238 || '''.556''' || '''1.5''' || '''1.5''' || '''.5''' || .1 || '''4.7''' |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee]] | 11 || 0 || 5.1 || .300 || .333 || {{sort|-|—}} || .5 || .5 || .3 || .0 || 1.3 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2024}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Phoenix Suns season|Phoenix]] | 16 || 0 || 7.4 || .311 || .190 || .500 || .8 || 1.0 || .2 || .0 || 2.2 |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A.
